correctness.rationale: For any constant-preserving linear averaging operator, telescoping step decomposition proves the induced BV norm equals the maximum variation among its n-1 single-step responses. Explicit integer edge counts are nonnegative and telescope to (n-1)/(n+1) for uniform intervals in every dimension. For length-first selection, exact rational all-cut computation independently matches two constructions for n=2..14, showing C_14=5105521/5045040 and no earlier C_n>1. Explicit continuum crossing integrals and bounded Riemann-sum convergence give liminf C_n >= 1+log(4/3). No finite sample is used to assert a general limit.

value.rationale: Two canonical uniform sampling laws on the same set of reversals have opposite variation-stability behavior: the all-interval average is sharply contractive for every n, while the length-first average first amplifies at the natural cutoff n=14 and stays bounded away from 1 asymptotically. This is a structural sampling-design distinction, with exact finite and analytic infinite witnesses, rather than a routine parameter substitution.
